interview.name: Tess
interview.answer: The repair drive is underway now, with drop-offs happening all morning at the organized location.

reflections: Tess is actively coordinating the repair drive and has become a reliable point person for updates.
Rey is willing to help and is waiting for a clearer need before stepping in.
Their exchange is practical and cooperative, centered on shared follow-through rather than formal planning.
Tess is a reliable coordinator who keeps everyone updated on the repair drive and follows through on checking what still needs to be done.
The others are supportive and ready to help once they have clear timing or task details, showing a cooperative volunteer dynamic.
Jules and Tess are helping organize the logistics, with Jules handling the drop-off flow and Tess relaying needs back to the group.
Tess is the main coordinator, repeatedly promising to check on needs later and relay updates to others.
Jules, Gus, and Rosa are responsive helpers who keep tasks organized and offer concrete support like supplies and updates.
The group is collaborating around a repair drive with a practical, ongoing need for hands, haul-offs, and organized drop-off logistics.
Tess is the central coordinator, relaying status and next steps to multiple people.
The group is responsive and collaborative, with neighbors offering hands, hauling help, and updates.
Oren benefits from clear, concrete scheduling updates when plans change.
Tess is the central coordinator who keeps everyone updated and follows through on logistics.
Rosa supports neighborhood communication and wants to stay informed about needed help.
Oren and Kira both want to help but need clear, repeated details about time and location to stay aligned.
